title: Is scl rational for chains in closed hyperbolic surface groups?
body:
## The question

Let S be a closed hyperbolic surface and let C be a chain in pi_1(S): a formal sum of
cyclically reduced conjugacy classes whose total homology class is trivial. Is scl(C)
always rational?

I conjecture that this is true, i.e. that scl(C) is always rational. This record is the 
top-level goal of the project; most other records bear on it.

The question is deliberately posed for chains and not merely for single group elements.
That is not a technical convenience forced by the definition; it is the right generality
to work in. Chains are what the cut-and-glue arguments actually produce and consume, and
a statement restricted to elements would have to be reformulated for chains at the first
step of any serious attempt.

Two things deliberately left open in the statement. First, whether it matters that S is
orientable is not known, and is recorded separately. Second, a declared variant of this
question asks the same thing for closed hyperbolic two-dimensional orbifolds, for
instance a torus with a single cone point of order 2; that variant is recorded
separately and is not a special case of the statement above.
